title: Canonical intrinsic realization of rational smooth purity
statement: Fix the datum $P$ of [def-pur-conventions] and the intrinsic rational/common-stage constructible categories of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a smooth separated morphism of pure dimension $d\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and fix a compactification $c$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements] and the coefficient-normalized constructible adjunction system $S$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Define the canonical realization $\gamma^{\mathrm{sf}}_{f,K}:Lf^*K(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}G(K)$ of the transported purity of [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity] in these intrinsic categories as follows. On the finite-Tor integral domain [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], transport the coefficient-unit orientation reconstructed in [thm-pur-adic-reconstruction], normalized by its finite diagonal traces. Use the coefficient line and quotient/root-normalized comparisons of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], [cor-pur-adic-and-rational-smooth-dualizing-complexes]. The finite integration is exactly the counit transpose of [def-pur-smooth-purity-map], [def-pur-smooth-trace] at the coefficient unit. For a general integral input form the projection/trace composite and transpose under the specified adjunction; its inverse is transported finite smooth purity. Localize this map with the coefficient mate of $S$. Its source comparison uses inverse localization commShiftIso at $2d$ on the shifted coefficient line followed by the integral tensor/pullback object formulas [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; it does not identify the rational and integral shift objects. For $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, use the literal finite field of each object, transport through the canonical small coefficient-model equivalence, and apply the common-stage exceptional comparison. Scalar source comparisons are the tensor, line, pullback and coherent shift comparisons, with the general scalar shift pinned at one and the existing common-stage transition shift retained. All coefficient associators and identity-transition unitors are retained. The canonical source and scalar/ordinary transports are those of [def-pur-canonical-purity-source-transports].

source.place: Proof sentence 3 (geometric orientation and trace) and sentence 4 (formal duality exchange from evaluation and adjunction maps)

proof.text: Construct finite integration and the uniquely finite-trace-normalized integral orientation as in the statement. For finiteDualizingPlus apply the existing etale bounded-below exceptional-image theorem to the bounded-below coefficient unit, using compactness of Y. For pullFiniteTor, integralSource_mem, and representativeTor use the equality of integral constructibility and integral finite Tor amplitude, and preservation by integral pullback and completed tensor. Uniqueness of the normalized orientation gives orientation_eq_adic and then the trace-transpose equality. Rationalize integralIso and compose with the specified exceptional mate. For ordinaryTensor_eq, first project the tensor clause of ordinaryModel_existsUnique at general coefficient parameters through the cached ordinaryMonoidal presentation, then specialize this API at the purity setting. The coefficient unit and left unitor use this same monoidal structure with the integral derived category explicit, retaining all unit and tensor normalizations. Small coefficient-model scalar associativity and Shrink.algEquiv inverse equations give the literal finite-stage transport and common-stage composite. Unfolding the published category-instance definitions proves their equality; transport the stage isomorphism along this equality before applying the common-stage inclusion. The six remaining named theorem obligations retain the complete proof plans in their Lean docstrings. The orientation, ordinary source, projection, integral isomorphism, and model-back scalar functor retain their original bodies with explicit return types in the canonical categories.

For rationalIntegralSource_eq, use the object clauses of rationalDerivedTensor_existsUnique and rationalDerivedPullback_existsUnique. Both rational operations preserve the displayed integral representatives. Reduce equality first to the integral full subcategory and then to its ambient objects. Apply the generic ambient-object formula for the inherited full-subcategory shift, proved by unfolding it in an abstract category; at the nonnegative exponent d the signed Tate line is the positive tensor power defining twist. The remaining tensor inputs agree definitionally. This preserves the specified localization shift comparison used by rationalSourceComparison.

For smoothPullAugmentation_isIso, work with an arbitrary coefficient field and separated, locally finite-type, quasi-compact morphism; the smooth-purity case is the required specialization. Apply finiteTorOrdinaryPullComplete to the ordinary completed-ring pullback of Q(C). The ambient augmentation comparison gives a module-pullback isomorphism and the exact chain-map identity. Its termwise extension and the derived pullback factorization present this complete ordinary object by the good ambient pullback complex. Apply canonicalCompletionUnitCriterion to make its specified completion unit invertible. Naturality transports invertibility to Q of the ambient complex; completionUnit_existsUnique then makes Q(roosUnit) invertible. Compose with the actual Roos tower isomorphism and then with the termwise module-pullback isomorphism. The ambient augmentation identity identifies this composite with the specified FrobeniusCoefficientTwists.pullbackAugmentation. This closes the augmentation obligation without adding a new theorem hole; the six other obligations retain their recorded plans.

proof_origin.place: Section 6.5, ordinary pullback completeness and normalized Roos completion unit; existing canonical realization proof for the other clauses
